mode: V2 research only; not V1 production science
purpose: High-recall Elder Tree candidate calibration that avoids under-prescribing candidate coverage across forest biomes.

prior.interpretation: Targets for candidate selection from real detected canopy maxima; not a biological assertion that 15 trees/ha are ancient.
prior.spatial_rule: Preserve local clustering; do not force a geometric grid.

evidence.source: Nilsson et al. 2002, Forest Ecology and Management 161:189-204
evidence.finding: 10–20 living trees/ha with DBH >70 cm were suggested as typical for many central European and south Scandinavian virgin forests; boreal forests commonly had at least 20 living trees/ha with DBH >40 cm.

evidence.source: USDA Forest Service PNW old-growth criteria
evidence.finding: Some southwest Oregon old-growth community criteria require 6–8 very large/old live conifers per acre, equivalent to roughly 15–20 per hectare.

evidence.source: Vandekerkhove et al. 2018, Forest Ecology and Management
evidence.finding: Across European old-growth beech reference sites, very large tree densities of 5–20/ha were prevalent; one exceptional stand exceeded 30/ha.
Observed hollow-bearing:recruitment-tree ratios near 1:2.0–1:2.3; modeled 1:3 recruitment improved long-term persistence of the hollow resource.

limits: There is no established universal Elder Tree fraction that applies to every forest.
Density prior must be validated against biome-specific structure and known inventories.
CURRENT_ELDER_CANDIDATE and FUTURE_ELDER_CANDIDATE remain modeled classes unless independently verified.
No effect on Aquifer Recharge Potential.
